newsitem.title: USA: Wash. state senate passes tax package for stadium.
newsitem.headline: Wash. state senate passes tax package for stadium.

text.p: The Washington state Senate Wednesday narrowly passed a package of taxes to fund a new $425 million football stadium demanded by billionaire Paul Allen as part of his plan to buy the Seattle Seahawks.
In a bipartisan 25-23 vote, the Senate passed the tax package backed by Democratic Gov. Gary Locke and sent it to the House, which is not expected to vote before next week.
That would be after Allen's latest April 3 deadline, but officials with the billionaire's Football Northwest organisation indicated the date could be extended.

Allen paid $20 million for an option to purchase the National Football League team that expires in July, and he has threatened to walk away from the deal unless he gets a state commitment for a new stadium to replace the 21-year-old Kingdome in downtown Seattle.
Before Allen stepped in, the Seahawks current owner, real estate developer Ken Behring, attempted to move the team to California but was blocked by the league.
Under the plan passed by the senate, the stadium would be funded by lottery scratch ticket games, a wholesale tax on sports logo-bearing items, and taxes on stadium admissions and parking.
Allen, the multibillionaire co-founder of Microsoft Corp., would contribute $100 million toward the total project cost of $425 million.
Allen also has insisted that the plan be approved in a popular vote.
